question.text: How does a Docker container differ from a traditional virtual machine?

reference.answer: Containers virtualise at the OS level: they share the host kernel and package only the app and its dependencies, so they are lightweight, start in seconds and allow high density. VMs virtualise hardware via a hypervisor and run a full guest OS each, so they are heavier and slower to boot but give stronger isolation.

keyPoints.text: Containers share the host OS kernel; VMs run a full guest OS
Containers are lightweight and start much faster
VMs use a hypervisor to virtualise hardware

answer: A Docker container shares the kernel of the host operating system, while a virtual machine has its own full operating system. Because of this containers are much lighter and they start in a few seconds. Containers are also more secure than VMs because they are fully isolated from each other.
